title: VPC offline upgrade sequencing and minimal egress contract
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define clear requirements and acceptance criteria for performing software upgrades to Redwood Private (VPC/air-gapped) installations with constrained or zero egress. This ticket codifies networking contracts, allowed upgrade sequencing, artifact distribution methods, and fallback/rollback expectations for customers operating in isolated networks.

Background: Several enterprise and regulated customers operate Private deployments with strict egress policies or physical-media-only update windows. Past incidents showed ambiguity around when operators can rely on mirrors, what metadata must be signed and verifiable offline, and acceptable outage windows during schema/DB migrations. This PRD closes gaps and establishes a minimal network contract for automated and semi-automated upgrade paths, plus explicit acceptance criteria for CI/QA to validate upgrades in isolated environments.
non_goals: Re-architecting the entire agent bootstrap flow or introducing new runtime protocols. This ticket does not change public-hosted upgrade flows or Dedicated reserved-capacity behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Offline artifact verification: Upgrade artifacts (images and operator manifests) required for Private installs must be digitally signed. A deterministic verification process (signature check, provenance hash) must succeed without outbound network calls. Test: provide signed artifacts and demonstrate successful install on a fully-isolated cluster.

2) Staged mirror workflow: Customers may provide an internal mirror server accessible from the VPC. The platform must support a mirrored upgrade path where controller nodes can fetch artifacts from a configurable internal HTTP(S) endpoint. Test: configure internal mirror and complete upgrade end-to-end.

3) Zero-egress bootstrap: For air-gapped installs that prohibit egress entirely, the platform must support an offline bundle (tarball + signed metadata) that operators can apply using the CLI. Test: complete install and upgrade using only the offline bundle and local registry.

4) Minimal connectivity contract: Define and document the minimal egress endpoints and ports required for the 'reduced-egress' automated upgrade path (metadata-only endpoints, certificate revocation lists). If customer disallows these, automated upgrades are considered "manual" and must follow the offline bundle path. Test: run a connectivity verification tool against a customer-like VPC to validate policy.

5) Rollback safety and checkpoints: Upgrades must include automatic pre-upgrade snapshots for control-plane state and a validated rollback procedure that completes without outbound network access. Test: simulate a failed upgrade and execute rollback to previous stable state within the documented RTO.

6) KMS/key rotation compatibility: For customers using KMS in-VPC or HSM, upgrades must not require re-encrypting stored model cache artifacts in a way that forces egress. Test: rotate a customer KMS key in a staged environment and validate runtime continues to decrypt cached artifacts post-upgrade.

7) Upgrade window and outage SLOs: For fully-isolated clusters the acceptance criteria must list expected disruption windows per upgrade category (minor: <5 minutes per node; major: rolling nodes with <30 minutes aggregate control-plane impact). Tests: run a timed upgrade exercise on a representative cluster and measure observed interruptions.
scope_changes: Initial scope included a managed background puller service for mirrors; removed due to scope/time constraints. Instead, this ticket defines the mirror API and operator checklist for customers to run their own mirror behind the firewall. Also narrowed automatic schema migrations: complex DB migrations that may require extended locks are out-of-scope for automated zero-egress upgrades and will require a documented manual migration runbook.
risks: Customers may misconfigure mirror TLS leading to silent signature bypass if operators disable verification
Rollback complexity with large KV cache sizes may exceed RTOs
Edge-case: dependency on time sync (NTP) for signature validation if clocks drift in air-gapped sites
implementation_notes: Engineering will deliver: 1) CLI flag --offline-bundle that consumes tar+signed-metadata, 2) mirror configuration schema (mirror_url, tls_ca, auth_token optional), 3) connectivity-check utility to validate minimal-egress policy, 4) pre-upgrade snapshot hook and documented rollback commands. QA will produce repeatable upgrade tests: mirror-based, offline-bundle, and reduced-egress variations. Security will review signature formats and KMS interactions prior to release.
